scope: Actual buffered/plain replay Source and append Appender dispatch establish Device/Writer contracts under explicit File/Buffer/Barrier/Hooks primitives. Native thin wrappers, snapshot freshness and outer lock/open/run correspondence remain open.
runtime_changes: wal_file uses the verified generic Source/Appender through native primitive wrappers. Existing payload allocation/copying, buffer capacity, I/O calls and fault points are preserved. Source rejects direct buffered truncate/sync calls that violate the existing interface preconditions and arms read uncertainty before allocation. No extra whole-log buffer or new performance campaign; no zero-overhead claim.

properties.wal_source::Source::from_file: Establishes explicit validity, available snapshot and unconsumed barrier, with exact file identity/bytes/logical cursor/durability.
properties.wal_source::Source::{length,read,discard: Maintains valid owned input and cached length when available. Returning failures of read/truncate/seek preserve quarantine; sync failure with a supplied barrier quarantines. Buffer extraction preserves identity/content/durability and exposes an arbitrary physical cursor; successful seek establishes the requested position and restores input on error. The supplied synchronization callback is consumed once.
properties.wal_sink::Appender::{from_file,inspect,w: Projects one raw file into an unbuffered Writer, observes exact position/length, writes the supplied span and dispatches existing queue/catalog barriers and hooks. Successful hooks preserve file context; all returning errors preserve identity while allowing effects.
properties.wal_device::{read_matches,empty_read_mat: Empty reads return an empty sequence without requiring cursor <= length; all nonempty successes retain exact bounds and bytes. The empty-read witness prevents an overstrong EOF assumption.
properties.wal_recovery / catalog_target / journal_: Actual generic recovery calls require and preserve DeviceModel::valid across every returned result, connecting Source construction to downstream framing/history/barrier composition.

specification_repair.problem: The old successful-read contract required cursor + length <= snapshot length even for zero-length reads. Native File and buffered zero-length reads can succeed past EOF.
specification_repair.evidence: Native regression seeks beyond EOF in buffered/plain modes, reads zero bytes successfully and checks unchanged file position/length; the Verus empty-read witness and its semantic negative check the corrected permission.
specification_repair.classification: Overstrong environment/adapter specification, not a production data-loss bug. No normal valid WAL framing behavior changed.

boundaries: ENV-FILE-PRIMITIVES retains native File/BufReader/Take/SHA and callback correspondence, snapshot consistency and correct opened-file/lock context. Generic dispatch proofs do not establish those wrappers or the OS implementation.
Logical buffered cursor and the physical cursor exposed by into_file differ; the extraction contract deliberately does not equate them. Final positioning is proved by the actual seek call.

Validity is explicit, established by Source construction and propagated by actual returning call chains. No no_unwind assumption or immutable File-view mutation axiom was added. Arbitrary unwinding is not proved; a native caught-barrier-panic test separately checks quarantine after a file effect.

No new trusted serde or collection primitive, admitted straw function or external proof body was added. All native implementation, compiler/allocator and complete distributed/GC obligations remain separately stated.

drafts_not_counted: Initial type-invariant approach required unsupported or no_unwind mutable-field operations. It was replaced by an explicit valid predicate with proved construction/preservation; no no_unwind assumption was introduced.

Initial mutually recursive File/Buffer trait bounds were rejected; Buffer only requires FileModel for its returned raw file, avoiding the cycle without weakening the required identity/content contract.
